story.head: Expect the Hurricanes to have the puck more
paras: The Hurricanes won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in Carolina on Oct 29. The Hurricanes have won three straight, while the Blue Jackets are winless in three (0-2-1). This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Jackets seventh (30th in the NHL) and the Hurricanes first (second).

The Blue Jackets have played better than their record (.396) says: their chances are worth about .512, and their finishing has held them back. The Hurricanes’ record (.820) is about what their chances are worth.

The Blue Jackets get their defensemen shooting (2nd) and forecheck as hard as almost anyone (2nd). Columbus has scored 2.33 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Hurricanes take away shots from the point (lowest) and create more chances on the penalty kill than anyone (1st), but give up a lot of dangerous shots (32nd). Carolina has scored 4.12 goals a game, the most in the league, and allowed 2.20, the fewest. The Hurricanes’ power play (7th) could do real damage against the Blue Jackets’ penalty kill (22nd). On top of that, the Hurricanes roll four lines, but the Blue Jackets lean on their top six.

Kent Johnson (9 G / 14 A / 23 P in 24 GP) leads the Blue Jackets in scoring, and Zach Werenski (5 G / 16 A / 21 P in 24 GP) is next in line. Sebastian Aho (13 G / 21 A / 34 P in 25 GP) leads the Hurricanes in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL. Logan Stankoven (11 G / 13 A / 24 P in 25 GP) isn’t far behind, with five goals in seven games against Columbus since 2023-24.

Cam Talbot (7-5-1 / .906 SV% in 13 GS) will likely start for Columbus. Carolina has two options in net: Pyotr Kochetkov (13-1-1 / .910 SV% in 15 GS) and Brandon Bussi (6-2-2 / .891 SV% in 10 GS). Kochetkov has started six of their last ten games, but Bussi got the last one on Nov 25. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

At home, Rod Brind'Amour likes to send Kotkaniemi, Jankowski and Robinson out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Lomberg, Lundeström and Pyyhtiä. One more thing: the Hurricanes usually control more of the chances than the Blue Jackets do.
